records.source: Δικαιωθέντες οὖν ἐκ πίστεως εἰρήνην ἔχομεν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ οὗ καὶ τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἐσχήκαμεν τῇ πίστει εἰς τὴν χάριν ταύτην ἐν ᾗ ἑστήκαμεν, καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ·
records.gloss: Having been justified therefore by faith peace we have toward the God through the Lord of us Jesus Christ, \v 2 through whom also the access we have had by the faith into the grace this in which we stand, and we boast on hope of the glory of the God;
pieces: So now that we have been declared righteous by faith, we are at peace with God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we have also been brought by faith into this grace where we now stand, and we boast in the hope of sharing God's glory.

L.1: Therefore, having been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}},
L.2: through whom we have also had access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we boast in hope of the glory of God.

R.1: God has made us right with {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} through faith. So now there is peace between God and us, through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
R.2: Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we have come by faith into God's grace, and we stand firm in it. And we rejoice, because we have the hope of sharing in God's glory.

decisions.choice: "we have peace": a statement
alternatives: "let us have peace with God" (an encouragement)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads the indicative, "we have". Many early and important manuscripts read the subjunctive, "let us have peace", which differs by one vowel; the two sounded alike when read aloud, so copyists easily confused them. The statement fits the argument: Paul is describing what God has done for those declared righteous, and verses 2-11 go on in statements. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: peace with God: the end of hostility between God and people
decisions.reason: The peace is not first a feeling of calm but a changed relationship: those who were God's enemies (verse 10) are now reconciled to him. It is the peace of the Hebrew shalom, wholeness and well-being given by God.

decisions.choice: therefore: drawing the conclusion of chapters 3-4
decisions.reason: "Having been justified by faith" gathers up what Paul has shown in 3:21-4:25, that God declares righteous those who believe, as he did Abraham. Chapter 5 now says what follows from it.

decisions.choice: access: being brought into the presence of a king or of God
decisions.reason: prosagōgē is the right of approach, the way in to someone of high rank. Paul uses it in Ephesians 2:18 and 3:12 of coming to the Father. The perfect "we have had" means the access was given and remains.

decisions.choice: "by faith" stands in the text
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts leave out "by faith" in verse 2, and others read "in faith". The SBLGNT keeps "by faith". The meaning is the same either way, since verse 1 has already said it. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: boast: glory in, take proud confidence in
decisions.reason: kauchaomai is to boast or to glory in something. In 2:17, 2:23 and 3:27 Paul rejected boasting in the law and in one's own works; here the believer's boasting rests on what God will do, as in Jeremiah 9:23-24, "let the one who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me" (Jeremiah 9:22-23 in the Hebrew numbering).

decisions.choice: the hope of the glory of God: hope of sharing God's glory
decisions.reason: In 3:23 all "fall short of the glory of God". The hope here is that believers will share that glory when God completes their salvation (8:17-18, 8:21, 8:30).

decisions.choice: declared righteous (B); made right with God (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:13, 3:24 and 4:2: Literal keeps "justified", Balanced says what the word means in a court, and Readable says what it means for the person, made right with God.

decisions.choice: the hope of sharing (in) God's glory
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the hope is, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: rejoice
decisions.reason: To a young reader, "boast" sounds like showing off. Readable says "rejoice" for this boasting in what God does, here and in verses 3 and 11; Literal and Balanced keep "boast", so that the link with 2:17-23 and 3:27 can be seen.

records.heading: At peace with God through faith

records.source: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμεθα ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσιν, εἰδότες ὅτι ἡ θλῖψις ὑπομονὴν κατεργάζεται, ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ δοκιμήν, ἡ δὲ δοκιμὴ ἐλπίδα.
records.gloss: Not only and, but also we boast in the troubles, knowing that the trouble endurance produces, \v 4 the and endurance proven character, the and proven character hope.
pieces: More than that, we boast even in our troubles, because we know that trouble leads to endurance,
endurance to proven character, and proven character to hope.

L.3: And not only [that], but we also boast in the troubles, knowing that trouble produces endurance,
L.4: and endurance, proven character, and proven character, hope.

R.3: And that is not all. We rejoice even when we have troubles. We know that troubles teach us to keep going.
R.4: When we keep going, we are tested and shown to be genuine. And that gives us hope.

decisions.choice: troubles: hardship and pressure of every kind
decisions.reason: thlipsis is pressure, distress, affliction. Paul uses it of the hardships believers suffer for their faith and in a fallen world (8:35, 2 Corinthians 4:17), and in 2:9 of the distress that comes on evildoers.

decisions.choice: endurance: holding out under pressure
decisions.reason: hypomonē is staying under a load without giving way: steadfast, patient endurance, not mere waiting (2:7, 8:25, 15:4).

decisions.choice: proven character: the quality of having been tested and found genuine
decisions.reason: dokimē is the result of a test, the approval of something that has stood it, like metal tried in the fire (2 Corinthians 2:9, 8:2, Philippians 2:22). Endurance in trouble shows that a person's faith is real.

decisions.choice: not only that: the boasting of verse 2 goes further
decisions.reason: The short phrase refers back to verse 2: believers boast not only in the hope of glory but even in present troubles, because of what the troubles produce.

decisions.choice: rejoice
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the chain of three steps
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the verb in the second and third steps. Balanced lets "leads to" carry over; Readable spells the steps out in short sentences.

records.source: ἡ δὲ ἐλπὶς οὐ καταισχύνει· ὅτι ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκκέχυται ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου τοῦ δοθέντος ἡμῖν.
records.gloss: The and hope not puts to shame, because the love of the God has been poured out in the hearts of us through Spirit Holy the [one] having been given to us.
pieces: And hope does not leave us ashamed, for God has given us the Holy Spirit, and through the Spirit {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love has flooded our hearts.

L.5: And hope does not put [us] to shame, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through [the] Holy Spirit who was given to us.

R.5: This hope will never let us down. God has filled our hearts with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love by giving us the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: hope that does not end in shame: Psalm 22:6 and 25:20
decisions.reason: In the Psalms, those who trust in God "are not put to shame" (Psalm 22:6, 25:20 in the Hebrew numbering; Isaiah 28:16, quoted in 9:33 and 10:11). To be put to shame is to have one's hope fail before everyone, above all at God's judgment. The hope of believers will not fail them.

decisions.choice: the love of God: God's love for us
decisions.reason: The phrase could mean our love for God, but verse 8 speaks of God's love for us, shown in Christ's death, and the hope rests on that love, not on ours.

decisions.choice: poured out: given richly
decisions.reason: The verb recalls the promise that God would pour out his Spirit (Joel 3:1-2 in the Hebrew numbering, Acts 2:17-18, 2:33). The perfect tense says the love was poured out and is still there.

decisions.choice: who was given: a single past gift
decisions.reason: The aorist points to the time believers received the Spirit when they came to faith (8:9, Galatians 3:2).

decisions.choice: has flooded (B); has filled (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "poured out" pictures: God's love given in full measure. Both make God the giver of the Spirit, as the passive "who was given" implies, and Balanced repeats "the Spirit" rather than use a pronoun.

decisions.choice: will never let us down
decisions.reason: Readable puts "put to shame" in everyday words: the hope will not turn out to be false.

records.source: Ἔτι γὰρ Χριστὸς ὄντων ἡμῶν ἀσθενῶν ἔτι κατὰ καιρὸν ὑπὲρ ἀσεβῶν ἀπέθανεν.
records.gloss: Still for Christ, being us weak, still according to time on behalf of ungodly died.
pieces: While we were still helpless, at the time God had chosen, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for the ungodly.

L.6: For while we were still weak, yet at the right time, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} died for [the] ungodly.

R.6: We had no strength to save ourselves. But when the time that God chose had come, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for us, even though we did not honor God.

decisions.choice: weak: without strength to save ourselves
decisions.reason: asthenēs is weak or sick. Here it describes people unable to do anything about their sin and their standing before God. Verses 8 and 10 say the same people were "sinners" and "enemies".

decisions.choice: at the right time: the time God set
decisions.reason: "According to time" means at the appointed or fitting moment, as in Galatians 4:4, "when the fullness of time came". The time was God's choice.

decisions.choice: "still" twice
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has "still" both at the start and before "at the right time". The second repeats and strengthens the first; some manuscripts smooth the sentence by changing or dropping one of them. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)

decisions.choice: for the ungodly: on behalf of people who did not honor God
decisions.reason: hyper is "on behalf of, for the sake of". The ungodly are the same "we": in 4:5 God "justifies the ungodly".

decisions.choice: the time God had chosen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose time it was, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: no strength to save ourselves; for us, even though we did not honor God
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of weakness is meant and that the ungodly are "us", as verses 8 and 10 make clear.

records.heading: God's love shown while we were sinners

records.source: μόλις γὰρ ὑπὲρ δικαίου τις ἀποθανεῖται· ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ τάχα τις καὶ τολμᾷ ἀποθανεῖν·
records.gloss: Scarcely for on behalf of righteous [one] someone will die; on behalf of for the good [one] perhaps someone even dares to die;
pieces: It is rare for anyone to give their life even for a righteous person; for a good person, perhaps, someone might find the courage to die.

L.7: For scarcely will anyone die for a righteous [person]; for perhaps for the good [person] someone might even dare to die.

R.7: It is rare for someone to die even for a person who does what is right. Someone might perhaps be brave enough to die for a person who is good and kind.

decisions.choice: righteous and good: an upright person and a generous benefactor
alternatives: the two words mean almost the same, and the second sentence corrects the first
"the good" as a thing: someone may dare to die for a good cause
decisions.reason: Paul sets two kinds of people side by side. The righteous person is just and upright; "the good" person (with the article) is most likely someone kind and generous, perhaps one's own benefactor, for whom gratitude might move someone to die. Either way, dying for anyone is rare, and Christ died for the ungodly.

decisions.choice: might even dare: a rare possibility
decisions.reason: "Perhaps" and "even dares" mark it as an exception: a few have been brave enough to die for a good person.

decisions.choice: give their life
decisions.reason: "Their" refers back to "anyone", as in everyday speech, and keeps the sentence for men and women alike.

decisions.choice: good and kind
decisions.reason: Readable shows the difference between the two people, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: συνίστησιν δὲ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἀγάπην εἰς ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔτι ἁμαρτωλῶν ὄντων ἡμῶν Χριστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀπέθανεν.
records.gloss: Shows but the of himself love toward us the God, that still sinners being us Christ on behalf of us died.
pieces: But God proves how much {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves us: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for us when we were still sinners.

L.8: But God shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own love for us in that while we were still sinners, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} died for us.

R.8: But God shows us how much {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves us. We were still sinners, and yet {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for us.

decisions.choice: shows: proves, gives evidence
decisions.reason: synistēmi here is to show clearly or demonstrate, as in 3:5. The present tense means the cross keeps showing God's love.

decisions.choice: God's love is shown in Christ's death
decisions.reason: Paul says God shows his own love through Christ's death, so Christ's dying is God's own act of love, not an act that wins God over (8:32, 2 Corinthians 5:19).

decisions.choice: while we were still sinners
decisions.reason: The love came before any change in us: Christ died for people still in their sins, as verse 6 has said.

decisions.choice: proves how much he loves us
alternatives: shows his own love for us
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "his own love" into a clause and lets the colon do the work of "in that".

records.source: πολλῷ οὖν μᾶλλον δικαιωθέντες νῦν ἐν τῷ αἵματι αὐτοῦ σωθησόμεθα δι’ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀργῆς.
records.gloss: By much therefore more, having been justified now by the blood of him, we will be saved through him from the wrath.
pieces: Since we have now been declared righteous by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, it is all the more certain that we will be saved through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from God's wrath.

L.9: Much more then, having now been justified by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, we will be saved through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the wrath.

R.9: We have now been made right with God because {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} shed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood for us. So we can be even more sure that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save us from God's anger.

decisions.choice: his blood: Christ's death as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: "Blood" stands for Christ's death, and recalls the blood of sacrifices (3:25). "By" gives the means: his death is how God declared us righteous.

decisions.choice: the wrath: God's judgment to come
decisions.reason: "The wrath" is God's coming judgment against sin (1:18, 2:5, 2:8, 1 Thessalonians 1:10). The future "we will be saved" looks to that day.

decisions.choice: much more: an argument from the greater to the lesser
decisions.reason: If God has already done the harder thing, declaring sinners righteous at the cost of his Son's blood, then he will surely do the rest. Paul uses the same argument in verses 10, 15 and 17.

decisions.choice: God's wrath (B); God's anger (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose wrath it is. Readable uses "anger", as in 1:18.

decisions.choice: shed his blood for us
decisions.reason: Readable says what "by his blood" refers to: Christ's death for us.

records.source: εἰ γὰρ ἐχθροὶ ὄντες κατηλλάγημεν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, πολλῷ μᾶλλον καταλλαγέντες σωθησόμεθα ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: If for enemies being we were reconciled to the God through the death of the Son of him, by much more having been reconciled we will be saved by the life of him;
pieces: We were enemies of God when the death of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son reconciled us to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Now that we are reconciled, it is all the more certain that we will be saved by the Son's life.

L.10: For if, being enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, much more, having been reconciled, we will be saved by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life.

R.10: We were God's enemies. But God made us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} friends again through the death of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. Now that we are God's friends, we can be even more sure that the Son, who is alive, will save us.

decisions.choice: enemies: hostile to God and under his displeasure
decisions.reason: echthros can be active (hostile to God, 8:7) or passive (treated by God as an enemy, 11:28). Both are true of people in their sin; reconciliation ends the hostility on both sides, though God is the one who acts.

decisions.choice: reconciled: brought from hostility into friendship
decisions.reason: katallassō is to change enmity into friendship. In Paul, God is always the one who reconciles and people are reconciled to him (2 Corinthians 5:18-20).

decisions.choice: by his life: by the risen life of the Son
alternatives: in his life: by sharing his life
decisions.reason: The Son who died now lives (6:9-10, 8:34); his life secures the final salvation of those reconciled by his death. en can mean "by" or "in" (sharing his life); both point to the living Christ.

decisions.choice: made us his friends again; God's friends
decisions.reason: Readable says what "reconcile" means, as 11:15 does. Literal and Balanced keep "reconcile".

decisions.choice: the Son's life (B); the Son, who is alive (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that "his" refers to the Son, and Readable that his life is his risen life.

records.source: οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δι’ οὗ νῦν τὴν καταλλαγὴν ἐλάβομεν.
records.gloss: Not only and, but also boasting in the God through the Lord of us Jesus Christ, through whom now the reconciliation we received.
pieces: More than that, we boast in God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} this reconciliation is now ours.

L.11: And not only [that], but [we are] also boasting in God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.

R.11: And that is not all. We rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, God has now brought us back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} friends.

decisions.choice: boasting: a participle with the force of a main verb
decisions.reason: Paul continues with a participle, "boasting", where a main verb is expected. It carries on the thought of verse 10: not only will we be saved, but we boast in God now.

decisions.choice: boasting in God
decisions.reason: Believers boast not in themselves or in the law (2:17, 23) but in God, as Jeremiah 9:23-24 and Psalm 34:3 (in the Hebrew numbering) call people to do.

decisions.choice: now received the reconciliation
decisions.reason: Reconciliation is something received as a gift, not achieved; "now" sets the present gift against the salvation still to come (verse 10).

decisions.choice: rejoice; brought us back to himself as his friends
decisions.reason: As in verses 2-3 and 10, and as 11:15 says "brought back to God and made friends with him".

records.source: Διὰ τοῦτο ὥσπερ δι’ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἡ ἁμαρτία εἰς τὸν κόσμον εἰσῆλθεν καὶ διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατος, καὶ οὕτως εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὁ θάνατος διῆλθεν ἐφ’ ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον ἄχρι γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία ἦν ἐν κόσμῳ, ἁμαρτία δὲ οὐκ ἐλλογεῖται μὴ ὄντος νόμου, ἀλλὰ ἐβασίλευσεν ὁ θάνατος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ μέχρι Μωϋσέως καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς μὴ ἁμαρτήσαντας ἐπὶ τῷ ὁμοιώματι τῆς παραβάσεως Ἀδάμ, ὅς ἐστιν τύπος τοῦ μέλλοντος.
records.gloss: Because of this, just as through one man the sin into the world entered, and through the sin the death, and so to all men the death passed through, on which all sinned \v 13 until for law sin was in world, sin but not is counted not being law; \v 14 but reigned the death from Adam until Moses even over the [ones] not having sinned in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of the [one] coming.
pieces: Therefore, just as through one man sin came into the world, and death came by sin, and so death reached all {{gender:people|men}} because all sinned—
for sin was already in the world before the law was given, but where there is no law, sin is not entered in the account.
Even so, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over people whose sin was not like Adam's breaking of a command. And Adam is a pattern of the one who was to come.

L.12: Therefore, just as through one man sin entered into the world, and through sin death, and so death spread to all {{gender:people|men}}, because all sinned—
L.13: for until [the] law, sin was in [the] world, but sin is not counted where there is no law;
L.14: yet death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of the one who was to come.

R.12: Sin came into the world because of one man, Adam, and sin brought death with it. So death came to everyone, because everyone sinned.
R.13: Sin was in the world even before God gave the law to Moses. But when there is no law, sin is not written down against anyone.
R.14: Still, death ruled over everyone from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. It ruled even over people who had not disobeyed a direct command of God as Adam did. Adam was a picture of someone who was going to come later: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: "just as" is left unfinished: Paul breaks off and completes the comparison in verse 18
alternatives: the comparison is completed within verse 12: "and so death spread to all"
decisions.reason: Paul begins a comparison, "just as through one man ...", but stops at the end of verse 12 to explain how sin and death worked before the law. The "so also" half comes in verses 18-19. The SBLGNT marks the break with a dash.

decisions.choice: because all sinned
alternatives: with the result that all sinned
on the basis of which (death) all sinned
decisions.reason: eph' hō is most likely "because", as in 2 Corinthians 5:4 and Philippians 3:12. Death came to all because all sinned. How the sin of all is related to Adam's sin Paul explains in verses 18-19: through one man's disobedience the many were made sinners. The Latin translation read the words "in whom" (in Adam all sinned), which shaped later teaching on original sin; the Greek does not say "in whom" without strain, since the nearest masculine noun is far back.

decisions.choice: sin and death as powers that enter and rule
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of sin and death as if they were rulers who entered the world and took control ("death reigned", verses 14 and 17; "sin reigned", verse 21; 6:12-14). Death here is both bodily death and separation from God, the opposite of the life of verses 17-21.

decisions.choice: sin is not counted where there is no law
decisions.reason: Without a written law, sin is not entered in the account as the breaking of a known command (4:15, "where there is no law there is no transgression"). Yet people died, which shows that sin was there and was deadly before Moses.

decisions.choice: not like Adam's transgression: not breaking a direct command
decisions.reason: Adam broke a spoken command of God (Genesis 2:17). People between Adam and Moses sinned, but not by breaking a command given to them in words. parabasis is the overstepping of a stated command.

decisions.choice: a type of the one who was to come: a pattern pointing to Christ
alternatives: "what was to come": the coming age
decisions.reason: typos is a mark or pattern that something else matches. Adam's act affected all who belong to him; Christ's act affects all who belong to him (1 Corinthians 15:22, 45). "The one who was to come" is Christ, from Adam's point of view.

decisions.choice: one man: Adam
decisions.reason: The one man is Adam, named in verse 14, as the story of Genesis 3 tells it.

decisions.choice: the dash after "sinned"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep Paul's broken-off sentence, with the dash, so the reader can see that the comparison is completed later. Readable writes plain statements.

decisions.choice: all {{gender:people|men}}; everyone (R)
decisions.reason: "All people" means all human beings, so the gender setting applies. Readable says "everyone", which needs no setting. "One man" is Adam and has no setting.

decisions.choice: Adam; God gave the law to Moses; the Messiah
decisions.reason: Readable names the one man, says which law is meant (verse 14 names Moses), and says who "the one who was to come" is, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: entered in the account (B); written down against anyone (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a bookkeeping word, as in Philemon 18, "charge it to my account". Literal says "counted", as for the related verb in chapter 4.

records.heading: Through one man sin, through one man grace

records.source: Ἀλλ’ οὐχ ὡς τὸ παράπτωμα, οὕτως καὶ τὸ χάρισμα· εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι οἱ πολλοὶ ἀπέθανον, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἡ δωρεὰ ἐν χάριτι τῇ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τοὺς πολλοὺς ἐπερίσσευσεν.
records.gloss: But not as the trespass, so also the free gift; if for by the of the one trespass the many died, by much more the grace of the God and the gift in grace the [one] of the one man Jesus Christ to the many abounded.
pieces: But the trespass and the free gift are not alike. If many died because of one man's trespass, then far more has God's grace overflowed to the many, together with the gift given by the grace of the one man Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.15: But not as the trespass, so also the free gift [is]. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} overflow to the many.

R.15: But God's gift is not like Adam's sin. Many people died because one man sinned. But God's grace has overflowed to many people even more. So has the gift that comes by the grace of one man, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: trespass: a false step, a wrong act
decisions.reason: paraptōma is a falling aside, a misstep: a specific wrong act, here Adam's disobedience. It is the word of 4:25 and is used throughout verses 15-20.

decisions.choice: free gift: a gift given out of grace
decisions.reason: charisma is a gift that comes from grace (charis), here God's gift of righteousness and life in Christ (6:23). dōrea is a gift freely given (3:24 has the related adverb, "freely").

decisions.choice: the many: all who belong to each one
decisions.reason: "The many" set against "the one" is a Hebrew way of saying "all", as verse 18 shows by saying "all people". It stresses how many were affected by one person's act, without saying how every one receives the gift (verse 17 speaks of "those who receive").

decisions.choice: much more: grace is greater than the trespass
decisions.reason: Here "much more" says not only that grace is more certain but that it is greater: it outweighs and overflows what the trespass did (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the trespass and the free gift are not alike
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the compressed Greek ("not as the trespass, so also the free gift") into a plain statement.

decisions.choice: Adam's sin; one man sinned
decisions.reason: Readable says "sin" for "trespass", a word young readers may not know, and names Adam, the one man of verses 12-14.

records.source: καὶ οὐχ ὡς δι’ ἑνὸς ἁμαρτήσαντος τὸ δώρημα· τὸ μὲν γὰρ κρίμα ἐξ ἑνὸς εἰς κατάκριμα, τὸ δὲ χάρισμα ἐκ πολλῶν παραπτωμάτων εἰς δικαίωμα.
records.gloss: And not as through one having sinned the gift; the indeed for judgment [was] from one to condemnation, the but free gift from many trespasses to justification.
pieces: Nor is the gift like what came through the one man who sinned. The judgment followed one trespass and brought condemnation, but the free gift followed many trespasses and brought acquittal.

L.16: And the gift [is] not as [what came] through one who sinned; for the judgment [came] from one [trespass] to condemnation, but the free gift from many trespasses to justification.

R.16: And God's gift does not work like what happened because of that one man's sin. After one sin came God's judgment, and it meant condemnation. But God's free gift came after many sins, and it puts people right with God.

decisions.choice: from one: from one trespass
decisions.reason: "From one" is most likely one trespass, set against "many trespasses" later in the verse. It could also be one man, as in the first half of the verse.

decisions.choice: justification: the verdict that declares righteous
decisions.reason: dikaiōma usually means a righteous requirement (1:32, 2:26, 8:4) or a righteous act (verse 18). Here it stands opposite "condemnation", so it is the opposite verdict: acquittal, being declared righteous.

decisions.choice: judgment and condemnation: a verdict and its sentence
decisions.reason: krima is the judge's decision; katakrima is the sentence of condemnation that follows (8:1).

decisions.choice: from many trespasses: grace answers all the sins that followed
decisions.reason: The judgment answered a single act; the gift answers the many sins of all people after it. That is the second way the gift is greater.

decisions.choice: acquittal
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the court word opposite "condemnation". Readable says "puts people right with God", as for "justify".

decisions.choice: God's judgment
decisions.reason: Readable says whose judgment it was.

records.source: εἰ γὰρ τῷ τοῦ ἑνὸς παραπτώματι ὁ θάνατος ἐβασίλευσεν διὰ τοῦ ἑνός, πολλῷ μᾶλλον οἱ τὴν περισσείαν τῆς χάριτος καὶ τῆς δωρεᾶς τῆς δικαιοσύνης λαμβάνοντες ἐν ζωῇ βασιλεύσουσιν διὰ τοῦ ἑνὸς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: If for by the of the one trespass the death reigned through the one, by much more the [ones] the abundance of the grace and of the gift of the righteousness receiving in life will reign through the one Jesus Christ.
pieces: If death reigned through one man because of that one man's trespass, it is far more certain that those who receive grace in full measure and the gift of righteousness will reign in life through the one man Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.17: For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one, much more those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life through the one, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.17: One man sinned, and because of that, death ruled as king through that one man. But God gives grace in rich measure, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives righteousness as a gift. So it is even more certain that those who receive this will live and rule as kings through one man, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: those who receive will reign: not life reigning, but people
decisions.reason: Paul does not say "life will reign", as the parallel with death would lead one to expect, but that people will reign in life. Those once ruled by death will themselves share Christ's rule (8:17, 2 Timothy 2:12). The future looks to the age to come, though the present participle "receiving" includes receiving now.

decisions.choice: the gift of righteousness: righteousness given as a gift
decisions.reason: The genitive tells what the gift is: righteousness, the right standing with God that he gives (3:21-22, 4:5).

decisions.choice: abundance: overflowing measure
decisions.reason: perisseia is a superabundance, more than enough; it echoes "overflowed" in verse 15.

decisions.choice: the sentence broken into three
decisions.reason: Readable states the two sides of the comparison in separate sentences and turns "those who receive the abundance of grace" into what God gives.

decisions.choice: ruled as king; live and rule as kings
decisions.reason: Readable says what "reign" means and turns "in life" into a verb, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: Ἄρα οὖν ὡς δι’ ἑνὸς παραπτώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς κατάκριμα, οὕτως καὶ δι’ ἑνὸς δικαιώματος εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἰς δικαίωσιν ζωῆς·
records.gloss: So then, as through one trespass to all men to condemnation, so also through one righteous act to all men to justification of life;
pieces: So then, as one trespass meant condemnation for all {{gender:people|men}}, so one righteous act means for all {{gender:people|men}} that they are declared righteous and given life.

L.18: So then, as through one trespass [the result was] condemnation for all {{gender:people|men}}, so also through one righteous act [the result is] justification of life for all {{gender:people|men}}.

R.18: So one sin brought condemnation on everyone. In the same way, one right action leads to people being made right with God and having life, and this is for everyone.

decisions.choice: the comparison begun in verse 12 is completed
decisions.reason: "As ... so also" picks up the "just as" of verse 12 and finishes it. The sentence has no verbs; the sense is supplied from verses 16-17.

decisions.choice: one trespass, one righteous act
alternatives: the trespass of one man; the righteous act of one man
decisions.reason: "One" agrees with the nouns, so the Greek most naturally means "one trespass" and "one righteous act", not "one man's". The one righteous act is Christ's obedience, above all in his death (verse 19, Philippians 2:8).

decisions.choice: justification of life: being declared righteous, which brings life
decisions.reason: dikaiōsis is the act of declaring righteous (4:25). "Of life" says what it leads to: the life of verse 17 and eternal life (verse 21).

decisions.choice: for all people: the gift as wide as the fall
alternatives: every person without exception will be declared righteous
decisions.reason: As Adam's trespass affected all, Christ's act is for all, with no one outside its reach. Verse 17 has said the reign in life belongs to "those who receive" the gift; Paul does not here explain how the two are related. The translation keeps "all" at every level.

decisions.choice: the result was (L); meant (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. Literal brackets the words it needs; Balanced uses "meant" and "means" to keep the past act and the present result.

decisions.choice: one right action; made right with God
decisions.reason: Readable says "right action" for the righteous act and "made right with God" for justification, as in verse 1.

records.source: ὥσπερ γὰρ διὰ τῆς παρακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου ἁμαρτωλοὶ κατεστάθησαν οἱ πολλοί, οὕτως καὶ διὰ τῆς ὑπακοῆς τοῦ ἑνὸς δίκαιοι κατασταθήσονται οἱ πολλοί.
records.gloss: Just as for through the disobedience of the one man sinners were made the many, so also through the obedience of the one righteous will be made the many.
pieces: For the disobedience of one man made the many sinners, and in the same way the obedience of the one will make the many righteous.

L.19: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were constituted sinners, so also through the obedience of the one the many will be constituted righteous.

R.19: Because one man disobeyed God, many people became sinners. In the same way, because one man obeyed God, many people will be made righteous.

decisions.choice: made: appointed, set in a standing
decisions.reason: kathistēmi is to appoint or put someone in a position (Acts 7:10, Titus 1:5). Through Adam the many were put in the standing of sinners; through Christ they will be put in the standing of the righteous. The word speaks of standing before God, and the next chapters show it also changes how they live.

decisions.choice: will be made: the future of God's final verdict and of all believers to come
alternatives: a logical future: will, as a consequence
decisions.reason: The future can point to the last judgment, when the verdict already given is confirmed, or to all who will yet believe. Both fit; Paul uses the future in the same way in verse 17.

decisions.choice: the obedience of the one: Christ's whole obedience, completed in his death
decisions.reason: Christ's obedience is his obedience to the Father, "to the point of death, even death on a cross" (Philippians 2:8). It reverses Adam's disobedience.

decisions.choice: the disobedience of one man made the many sinners
alternatives: the many were made sinners through the disobedience of one man
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the passive verbs into active ones, with disobedience and obedience as subjects.

decisions.choice: constituted (L); became, will be made (R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "constituted" for the legal sense of the verb; Readable says it simply.

records.source: νόμος δὲ παρεισῆλθεν ἵνα πλεονάσῃ τὸ παράπτωμα· οὗ δὲ ἐπλεόνασεν ἡ ἁμαρτία, ὑπερεπερίσσευσεν ἡ χάρις, ἵνα ὥσπερ ἐβασίλευσεν ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ, οὕτως καὶ ἡ χάρις βασιλεύσῃ διὰ δικαιοσύνης εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: Law and came in alongside so that might increase the trespass; where but increased the sin, overflowed beyond the grace, \v 21 so that just as reigned the sin in the death, so also the grace might reign through righteousness to life eternal through Jesus Christ the Lord of us.
pieces: The law came in alongside, so that the trespass would multiply. But where sin multiplied, grace overflowed far beyond it,
so that, as sin held its reign through death, grace in turn might reign through righteousness and lead to eternal life through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} our Lord.

L.20: And [the] law came in alongside so that the trespass might increase; but where sin increased, grace overflowed all the more,
L.21: so that, just as sin reigned in death, grace also might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} our Lord.

R.20: Then the law came in, so that wrongdoing would grow even more. But where sin grew, God's grace grew far more.
R.21: Sin ruled over people and brought them death. Now God's grace rules instead, through the righteousness God gives, and it leads to eternal life through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} our Lord.

decisions.choice: came in alongside: added to a situation already there
decisions.reason: pareiserchomai is to come in beside. The law of Moses came in after sin and death were already in the world (verses 13-14), as Galatians 3:19 says it "was added". It does not here mean coming in secretly.

decisions.choice: so that the trespass might increase: the law's purpose in God's plan
alternatives: with the result that the trespass increased
decisions.reason: hina most naturally gives purpose: the law made sin into open transgression of a command and so made it more and plainer (4:15, 7:7-13, Galatians 3:19). Some read it as result only.

decisions.choice: overflowed all the more: grace far beyond sin
decisions.reason: Paul adds a prefix to the verb "overflow" of verse 15 to make it stronger: grace overflowed beyond all measure.

decisions.choice: reigned in death: ruled by means of death
alternatives: sin reigned in the realm of death
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean sin ruled with death as its power and its result, or ruled in the realm of death. Grace, in contrast, rules "through righteousness" and leads to life.

decisions.choice: through righteousness: the righteousness God gives
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, righteousness is God's gift of right standing, and with it the righteous life it brings (chapter 6).

decisions.choice: multiply
decisions.reason: The same verb comes twice; Balanced keeps one word for both, so the reader sees grace answering sin.

decisions.choice: wrongdoing
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for "trespass", as for "sin" in verse 15.

decisions.choice: the righteousness God gives
decisions.reason: Readable says what the righteousness is, as the meaning decision explains.
